Subject: Physics | Chapter: Photoelectric effect and matter waves

QUESTION:
What should be the approximate kinetic energy of an electron so that its de-Broglie wavelength is equal to the wavelength of X-ray of maximum energy, produced in an X-ray tube operating at 24800 V ? (given that h = 6.6×10^(− 34) joule-sec, mass of electron = 9.1×10^(− 31) kg )

(A) 600 eV
(B) 365 eV
(C) 120 eV
(D) 300 eV

STORED ANSWER KEY: "A"

STORED SOLUTION:
We want the kinetic energy of an electron such that:
λ_(deB) = λ_(min)

For X-ray tube at accelerating potential V = 24,800 V :
λ_(min) = (hc)/(eV)

De-Broglie wavelength of electron:
λ_(deB) = h/(√(2mK))

Setting them equal:
h/(√(2mK)) = (hc)/(eV)

Cancel h :
1/(√(2mK)) = c/(eV)
√(2mK) = (eV)/c K& = (1.574×10^(− 29))/(1.638×10^(− 13))
K& ≈ 9.6×10^(− 17) J

Convert to eV :
K = (9.6×10^(− 17))/(1.6×10^(− 19)) ≈ 600eV
